title: 36th NATO Summit Opens in Ankara — Trump, Zelenskyy Among Attendees
detail: The 36th NATO Summit opened in Ankara on July 7, 2026 at President Erdoğan's Presidential Complex — only the second time Türkiye has hosted alliance leaders after the 2004 Istanbul summit. All 32 NATO member-state leaders attended alongside non-alliance guests Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and South Korean President Lee Jae-myung. Defense spending topped the agenda, with members committing to invest 5% of GDP in defense by 2035. Erdoğan held bilateral meetings with US President Trump, French President Macron, Finnish President Stubb, Slovak President Pellegrini and German Chancellor Merz, using the summit to press Türkiye's case as an indispensable NATO power controlling the Bosphorus Strait, İncirlik airbase access and NATO's second-largest standing military.

title: Trump Says US Will Lift CAATSA Sanctions on Türkiye, 'Consider' F-35 Sale
detail: Meeting Erdoğan on the sidelines of the NATO summit in Ankara on July 7, 2026, President Trump said the US would remove sanctions imposed on Türkiye under the Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (CAATSA) — imposed after Ankara's 2019 purchase of Russian S-400 air defense systems led to Türkiye's expulsion from the F-35 program. 'We're going to be taking the sanctions off; it's time,' Trump said, adding he would soon decide on resuming F-35 sales and calling the jet 'the best plane by far.' Erdoğan said he hoped for a 'favourable decision,' noting Türkiye had previously been promised five jets. Any return to the F-35 program still requires a presidential determination under a 2020 law that Türkiye no longer possesses or operates the S-400 system. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu publicly urged against the sale, saying it would upset the regional balance of power.

media.caption: Trump and Erdoğan meet on the sidelines of the NATO Ankara summit — July 7, 2026

confidenceReason: Trump's sanctions-lift statement is a verified public remark, but formal CAATSA delisting and any F-35 sale require further US government action not yet finalized.
